description: JavaScript / TypeScript dangerous-pattern rules. These are regex heuristics, not parsed analysis, so they are reported at medium confidence or lower - see modules/patterns.py for why that honesty matters.

rules.title: eval() on a non-literal value
rules.remediation: Remove eval(). For dynamic property access use a lookup object; for parsing use JSON.parse; for arithmetic use a real expression parser.

rules.title: new Function() builds code from a string
rules.remediation: `new Function` is eval with extra steps. Replace it with a closure or a dispatch table.

rules.title: Shell command built by interpolation
rules.remediation: Use execFile or spawn with an argument array so the shell is never involved: spawn('git', ['clone', url]). If you must use a shell, allowlist the input.

rules.title: spawn() with shell: true
rules.remediation: shell: true reintroduces metacharacter injection. Drop it and pass arguments as an array.

rules.title: innerHTML assigned a non-literal value
rules.remediation: Use textContent for text, or sanitise with DOMPurify before assigning HTML.

rules.title: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML
rules.remediation: Sanitise the HTML with DOMPurify first. The API is named this way on purpose.

rules.title: document.write() with dynamic content
rules.remediation: Build nodes with createElement/textContent instead.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.remediation: Never disable certificate validation outside a throwaway local test. To trust an internal CA, add it via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS instead.

rules.title: Math.random() used for a token or identifier
rules.remediation: Math.random is not cryptographically secure and is predictable across calls. Use crypto.randomBytes() or crypto.randomUUID().

rules.title: SQL query built with template interpolation
rules.remediation: Use parameterised queries: db.query('SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = $1', [id]). Interpolating into SQL is injection regardless of how the value looks today.

rules.title: SQL query built by string concatenation
rules.remediation: Use parameterised queries or a query builder that escapes for you.

rules.title: JWT decoded without verifying its signature
rules.remediation: jwt.decode does not check the signature - anyone can forge the payload. Use jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms allowlist.

rules.title: CORS wildcard origin combined with credentials
rules.remediation: A wildcard origin with credentials lets any site make authenticated requests as your users. Reflect an explicit allowlist instead.

rules.title: Redirect target taken from the request
rules.remediation: Validate the target against an allowlist of paths or hosts before redirecting.

rules.title: crypto.createCipher() is deprecated and insecure
rules.remediation: createCipher derives a key with MD5 and uses a zero IV. Use createCipheriv with a random IV and a properly derived key.

rules.title: Weak hash used for a password
rules.remediation: Use argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt. Fast hashes let an attacker try billions of candidates per second against a stolen table.

rules.title: bcrypt cost factor below 10
rules.remediation: Use a cost of at least 12 for new applications and re-hash on next login.

rules.title: postMessage() to a wildcard origin
rules.remediation: Name the exact target origin so the message cannot be read by an unexpected frame.

rules.title: Auth token stored in localStorage
rules.remediation: localStorage is readable by any script on the page, so one XSS becomes full account takeover. Prefer an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie.

rules.title: setTimeout/setInterval with a string body
rules.remediation: A string body is evaluated as code. Pass a function instead.

rules.title: Node vm module used as a sandbox
rules.remediation: Node's vm module is not a security boundary - escapes are well documented. Use a separate process with restricted permissions, or isolated-vm.

rules.title: Filesystem path built from request data
rules.remediation: Resolve the path and confirm it stays inside the intended directory: const p = path.resolve(base, name); if (!p.startsWith(base + path.sep)) reject.

rules.title: require() with a computed path
rules.remediation: A dynamic require can load an attacker-chosen module. Map allowed names to static imports.

rules.title: Recursive merge without prototype guards
rules.remediation: Reject __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys before merging, or use Object.create(null) for parsed data.

rules.title: Non-cryptographic UUID generation
rules.remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() - it is built in and actually random.
